summary:
We developed Moon & Mars Commander, an interactive 3D browser-based space survival and STEM education game built with Roblox studio for kids aged 7–12. Players step into the boots of a young astronaut tasked with keeping a lunar and Martian outpost alive for 100 space days alongside Orby, a friendly black-and-cyan sci-fi mech companion.

The game addresses the challenge of making real space science—such as low-gravity physics, resource scarcity, radiation shielding, and closed-loop life support—engaging and easy to understand for young learners. Players mine crater ice, space metal, and sun crystals to build Solar Arrays, Space Plant Farms, and Water Shield Domes across 10 outpost pads while balancing Oxygen, Water, Power, and Shield levels. By turning planetary survival into hands-on problem-solving, the project sparks curiosity in aerospace engineering, sustainability, and space exploration.
details:
Moon & Mars Space Base: 100-Day Deep Space Outpost, created by Team OrbitX, is an interactive 3D browser-based space habitat and deep-space flight simulator designed to let players experience the engineering challenges of living beyond Earth. The mission begins on Earth at Launch Complex 39B, where players enter their Commander name, select either the Moon (Tranquility Outpost) or Mars (Olympus Outpost), and initiate a 3-2-1 heavy rocket liftoff. Upon landing, players manage a 100-day survival mission across a connected multi-dome outpost equipped with automatic sensor-driven airlock doors, a central Command Hub, and a Base Control Computer (C) with an incoming hazard radar. Throughout realistic Day and Night cycles, players must balance four critical life-support vitals—Air (Oxygen), Water, Power, and Shielding—by constructing 50 functional space modules across 36 outpost pads spanning Power (Solar Panels, Star Reactors, Mega Batteries), Life Support (Algae Oxygen Tanks, Ice Drills, Space Farms), Defense (Meteor Lasers, Magnet Domes, Plasma Shields), Science, and Habitats. Players also practice In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) by walking to Crystal Mountain to drill Metal, Ice, and Energy Crystals with a mining laser (F), reinforcing their base with 3-tier Fortress upgrades (U) to withstand solar storms and meteor showers, and boarding the base’s delta-wing Space Shuttle (E) to lift off vertically (Space) into Deep Space orbit and travel between the Moon and Mars.

The primary benefit and intended impact of this project is making complex NASA aerospace concepts—such as closed-loop life support, solar-to-battery night power management, radiation shielding, and ISRU—intuitive, visual, and engaging for students, educators, and space enthusiasts. Because the entire experience runs inside a standard web browser with zero installations or downloads required, anyone can immediately explore how human habitats operate on the Moon and Mars.

To develop the project, Team OrbitX used HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript (ES6+) paired with the Three.js (WebGL) library for real-time 3D scene rendering, custom spatial collision detection, dynamic lighting, and procedural 3D geometry such as chamfered hulls, organic boulders, and crystal lathes. All surface details—including spacecraft hull plating, lunar and Martian crater bump maps, and hexagonal armor—were generated procedurally using the HTML5 Canvas API, while thruster, airlock, and laser sound effects were synthesized in real time using the Web Audio API. We also integrated the Web Speech API (SpeechSynthesis and SpeechRecognition) to power ORBY, a floating AI robot companion that guides players through mission objectives and responds to voice commands.

What makes our project especially creative is how it blends third-person planetary exploration, strategic base-building, vertical orbital shuttle flight, and an interactive voice-enabled robot buddy inside a single self-contained web file. In designing the simulation, our team carefully balanced technical accessibility with scientific realism: we kept the application lightweight with toggleable HUD controls (H) so it runs smoothly on everyday school or home computers, while modeling authentic off-world survival trade-offs—such as solar panels going offline during lunar and Martian nights—alongside an optional Free Build mode so learners of all ages can experiment freely.
